touches.text: Two callers waking the same part at once start only one: the part that binds its socket first is the only one; a second copy finds it taken and exits quietly (as the ground loop does, 5.6.4.3). [Q#93: Ticket b38af5fd1852 says a second live copy of a host singleton refuses LOUDLY; this line says it exits QUIETLY. Your words, 2026-11-12: "when it's going to spin up another, the act of spinning it up should either exit or close the other. what needs to be a singleton per cairn? cairn itself across all boxes. maybe codemother. but on an individual host, that would be the ground loop, the bus, the rack, there can't be two akienasus_cc_0 on the same bus! that would be akienasus_cc_1". Two choices: the second copy exits (loud or quiet), or it closes the first (supersede). Is the answer the same for the bus, the ground loop, the rack and a device name?]

What the waker starts outlives whoever started it (detached, or through systemd-run --user, which gives it its own memory cap and log while still deciding nothing). Restarting a shim never takes down the bus it once woke. [Q#92: A proof that starts Windows processes stays red until it has your word (CAIRN_PROOF_MAY_SPAWN=1). Measured 2026-11-12: tooth 2 of dc945eb1f072 (cairn.cmd against Git Bash) is red on exactly that word, and nothing in this outline says what the word is. Is it an env var each run sets, a standing flag in ~/.cairn, or may a proof spawn one short hidden process without asking?]
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.
Any shim, through its pulse.py, brings the bus up if it's down: whatever is called brings up what it needs (5.3.4.1).

One setup question: "Is this a cairn home? No? Then what's the hostname/IP for the cairn home I should attach to?" The answer is an env var (CAIRN_HOME_HOST), beside the ones for where the repo and the runtime folder are.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
